subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migration, should OpenClaw key/reset update offsets by `apiRoot`, rely on doctor/docs for manual reset, or keep the current account/token-only watermark behavior?
rationale: The source path is clear, but persisted offset ownership and the safe scope for tolerating `400: Logged out` are compatibility-sensitive runtime choices rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
options.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, add a narrow logged-out cleanup tolerance for migration, and require live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Doctor/docs reset only
options.body: Keep runtime account/token offsets unchanged and make `openclaw doctor --fix` or documentation the supported reset path when switching endpoints.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave local Bot API endpoint migration as an operator-managed advanced workflow and document the current manual cleanup expectations.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware runtime fix
recommendation.body: Scope or invalidate Telegram update offsets when `apiRoot` changes, add a narrow logged-out cleanup tolerance for migration, and require live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the Telegram polling/spool path makes this the best available routing owner for the runtime policy choice.
